newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina denies contacts with man linked to murder.
newsitem.headline: Argentina denies contacts with man linked to murder.

text.p: Argentina's Peronist government on Sunday rejected as "absolutely false" newspaper reports that officials met secretly with a businessman linked to a high-profile murder case.

Interior Minister Carlos Corach and President Carlos Menem's Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan both denied front-page reports in Argentina's two biggest newspapers, La Nacion and Clarin, of secret contacts with postal tycoon Alfredo Yabran.
Yabran has been linked to the brutal murder in January of news photographer Jose Luis Cabezas, and is to be questioned by a judge this week in connection with the case.
Saying "neither Yabran nor anyone else" is immune from investigation, Corach and Kohan told reporters the government had not tried to influence the case in favour of Yabran.
Corach denied that he and Yabran met for lunch during the Easter holiday in an Andean ski resort.
He also denied that Menem's former brother-in-law, Emir Yoma, acted as go-between for Yabran to complain to Menem about statements by officials linking him to the murder.

"I never had lunch with him, neither in San Martin de los Andes nor in any other part of the country, in my entire life," Corach told reporters. "From Menem down, we are all totally convinced it is necessary to investigate every single clue until this crime is cleared up once and for all."

Cabezas was handcuffed, beaten, shot and his body doused with fuel and burned to a charred skeleton. A gang led by former police officer Gustavo Prellezo has been arrested for the killing, but investigators are still hunting the "intellectual authors" behind the crime.
Phone calls made by Prellezo in the weeks just before the murder have been traced to the head of Yabran's personal bodyguard.

Yabran's reported friendship with Carlos Menem, as well as his alleged links with Corach, Kohan, Justice Minister Elias Jassan and many other powerful Peronist figures would make any proven link between him and Cabezas' killing a major embarrassment for the government, especially in an election year.

Yabran, accused by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo and opposition politicians of being the head of organised crime in Argentina -- charges he denies -- has been summoned for questioning on Friday by the judge investigating the murder of Cabezas, who worked for Noticias news magazine.
